fixes.explanation: Good guess, baker, but this passage never mentions a steward. It only says John heard about the works of Christ in prison and sent his disciples. They're the ones carrying the question, which makes this a very short list of messengers. No steward needed.

Nope, nobody asks about a visit. The question is about who Jesus is: "Are You the One who was to come, or should we look for someone else?" It's a question about His identity, not His travel plans. Nobody's asking Him to drop by with a cookie box, either.

Ooh, I see the thinking, baker, but the rich don't make this list. Jesus ends His report with "…the good news is preached to the poor." That's the last thing He tells John's disciples to carry back. So the word that fits is poor.

That's it, baker. Jesus says, "Blessed is the one who does not fall away on account of Me." That's how He wraps up His answer to John, who asked his question from prison. I think that's a tender thing to say to a man sitting in a cell. The blessing is for the one who does not fall away.

That's right. Jesus says, "Look, those who wear fine clothing are found in kings’ palaces." Palaces are the place He names for fine clothing. He's asking the crowds what they went out to see, and I love how He walks them through it.

City gates would be a busy spot to see people, but Jesus doesn't mention them here. He says, "Look, those who wear fine clothing are found in kings’ palaces." So the answer is palaces. Jesus asks the crowds what they went out into the wilderness to see, and palaces are the place He names for fine clothing.

That's right. Jesus says, "And if you are willing to accept it, he is the Elijah who was to come." Jesus says it plainly, and it comes with an "…if you are willing…" so He leaves it to the crowd to take it in.
Reasonable guess, baker, but Isaiah isn't the name Jesus gives here. He says, "…he is the Elijah who was to come." So the name in this verse is Elijah.

Jeremiah's a fair guess, but Jesus doesn't name him in this passage. He says, "…he is the Elijah who was to come." Elijah is the name on the card. I'd have taken a guess like yours, baker, but this time the answer is Elijah.

Jesus doesn't mention soldiers in this picture. He says they're "…children sitting in the marketplaces and calling out to others…" Picture kids calling out to others. Soldiers aren't part of what Jesus describes, so the answer is children.

Not this time. Jesus, the Son of Man, came eating and drinking, and they say, "Look at this glutton and drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!" So they still find something to say, and it isn't approval. Different way of coming, same story: they still have a complaint.
